OVERVIEW

Seven steps, from click to reply

Every "Get my quote" enquiry follows the same path. The system handles the first four steps on its own — Lyn's job starts at step 5, when the notification lands in her inbox.

1

Lead clicks "Get my quote"

On the homepage or the top nav of colliers.net.au.

2

Lead fills out the form

A 3-step form: occasion, contact details, then catering specifics.

3

Contact & opportunity created

A CRM contact and a New Enquiry opportunity appear automatically.

4

Lead gets an instant reply

An automatic confirmation email and SMS go out straight away.

5

Lyn is notified

An email lands with the lead's details and a direct CRM link.

6

Lyn replies from the CRM

Reply by SMS or email from inside the contact record, not from her own phone or inbox.

7

Move the opportunity to Contacted

Update the pipeline stage once the reply is sent, so the board stays accurate.

STEP 1 / colliers.net.au

Lead clicks "Get my quote"

Nothing for Lyn to do here

The button appears in two places: the top navigation bar, and the hero section of the homepage next to "Order online". Anyone enquiring about catering — rather than placing a straightforward online order — starts here.

STEP 2 / colliers.net.au/get-my-quote

Lead is taken to the form

Nothing for Lyn to do here

The lead is redirected to a 3-step form. It's short by design, so rough details are fine — Lyn confirms everything with the lead afterwards.

  1. Step 1 of 3 — What are you organising? Breakfast, morning/afternoon tea, office lunch, an event or function, regular office catering, or "not sure."
  2. Step 2 of 3 — Contact details. Name, company, work email, mobile number, and delivery postcode.
  3. Step 3 of 3 — The details. Date needed, delivery time, headcount, budget per person, food preferences, dietary requirements, one-off vs recurring, and free-text notes.
STEP 3 / GoHighLevel CRM

Contact & opportunity are created

Nothing for Lyn to do here

The moment the form is submitted, the system creates a contact record and tags it enquiry, form-quote-completed and lane-quote. An opportunity is created at the same time in the Sales Pipeline, sitting in the New Enquiry stage — named after the lead, with the date they need catering.

STEP 4 / Automatic email + SMS

The lead gets an instant reply

Nothing for Lyn to do here

Before Lyn even sees the enquiry, the lead already has confirmation that it's been received — by email ("Got your catering enquiry") and by SMS. This is what sets expectations, so it's worth knowing what the lead has already been told.

This is what the lead sees automatically: a short email, plus a text confirming the enquiry and that someone will follow up with options.
STEP 5 / Email

Lyn is notified

This is where Lyn's job starts

An internal notification email lands with the lead's details — name, phone, email, occasion, frequency, headcount — plus a direct link straight into the contact record in the CRM. There are three versions of this email, and which one is sent depends on how the enquiry is scored:

  1. 🎉 High Value Lead — subject line "High Value Lead," flagged with a party emoji so it stands out in the inbox.
  2. Mid Value Lead — subject line "Mid Value Lead," no emoji.
  3. 🔵 Low Value Lead — subject line "Low Value Lead," flagged with a blue dot.

How the tier is decided — the CRM checks the enquiry against these rules in order. Mid Value is the default: anything that doesn't match High or Low falls there.

🎉 High Value — any of

Matches if any one is true
  • Headcount is 100+
  • Occasion is "Regular weekly catering"
  • Order frequency is "Every few weeks"
  • Order frequency is "Weekly or more"

Mid Value — the default

Anything that doesn't meet a High Value or Low Value rule lands here. This is the most common tier — most "office lunch" and one-off enquiries end up Mid.

🔵 Low Value — any of

Matches if any one is true
  • Occasion is "Office lunch or meeting" and headcount is 15–30
  • Occasion is "Office lunch or meeting" and headcount is under 15
What to do: whichever version lands, click the CRM link in the email. It opens the exact contact record, so there's no searching for the lead. Treat the subject line as a priority signal — a High Value Lead is worth calling back first.
STEP 6 / GoHighLevel CRM

Lyn replies from the CRM

This is where Lyn's job starts

From the contact record, review what the lead asked for — occasion, headcount, budget, dietary needs — then reply by SMS or email from inside the CRM, using the message box at the bottom of the contact.

  1. Open the contact from the CRM link in the notification email.
  2. Check the details already on file — occasion, headcount, date, budget, dietary needs — under "All fields" and in the enquiry note.
  3. Reply using the message box at the bottom of the conversation, choosing SMS or email.
  4. Keep the reply inside the CRM rather than a personal phone or inbox, so the whole conversation stays logged on the contact.
Why it matters: replying from the CRM (not a personal phone) keeps the full conversation on the contact record, so anyone else picking up the enquiry later can see the full history.

STEP 7 / GoHighLevel CRM

Move the opportunity to Contacted

This is where Lyn's job starts

Once the reply has been sent, update the opportunity's stage in the Sales Pipeline — from New Enquiry to Contacted. This keeps the pipeline board accurate, so it's clear at a glance which leads still need a first response and which ones have already been followed up.

  1. From the contact record, open the opportunity (it's linked in the activity timeline, or under the Opportunities tab).
  2. Change the stage from New Enquiry to Contacted.
  3. Do this straight after sending the reply, not later — an opportunity left in New Enquiry looks unactioned even after Lyn has replied.
Why it matters: the pipeline stage is how anyone else — including CJ — can tell at a glance whether a lead has been followed up. Leaving it in New Enquiry makes a handled lead look untouched.
